description: A dark, oil-painting-style scene of a man in a wide-brimmed hat, brown doublet with a white collar, sash and bandolier, standing upright and holding a long musket. He stands in a grove of trees bearing yellow-orange fruit split open to show red seeds. Behind him, on a bay under a stormy sky, a three-masted sailing ship with large sails carrying a monogram-like emblem and a small flag at the masthead, with smaller boats and a dark headland on the left. A small white sparkle logo sits in the bottom-right corner. The painting fills the frame edge to edge.
reason: Shows a 17th-century Dutch East India-style sailing ship and a musketeer among spice trees, not the Japanese tea ceremony. The ship and flag date to after 1600, so they do not fit a Japanese setting in 1580. The sails carry a monogram that reads as letters (VOC-like), which breaks the no-text rule.
